## Example 5.2: Avoiding a reference state

Repeat the heat calculation of Example 5.1 without a reference state

::: {.content-visible unless-format="revealjs"}
::: {.callout-note icon=false collapse="true" title="Solution"}

The balance is unchanged from Example 5.1:

$$\dot{Q} = \dot{m}\left(H_{out} - H_{in}\right)$$

As $H_{out}-H_{in}$ is just a sensible heat change:

$$H_{out}-H_{in} = \Delta H = \int^T_{out}_T_{in} C_P dT$$

with $\dot{m}$= 0.50 kg s$^{-1}$ and $C_P = 1.01$ kJ kg$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ and constant with temperature
$$
\begin{aligned}
\dot{Q} & = \dot{m}\int^T_{out}_T_{in} C_P dT \\
        & \dot{m}C_P \int^T_{out}_T_{in} dT\\
        & = \dot{m}C_P (T_{out} - T_{in})\\
        & = 0.5 \cdot 1.01 \cdot (150 - 25)\\
        & = 63.125\ \mathrm{kW}
\end{aligned}
$$

The same answer as example 5.1 without using any reference state directly

:::
:::
